sentences.english_text: Outside in the park, the wind had returned for Drippy.
I'm back, little raindrop.
Let's, uh.
And he looked down at the park mensch and saw that Drippy was no longer there.
Drippy, where are you?
The wind whirled around the park, sending leaves and papers shooting into the air.
The wind looked everywhere, searching for Drippy, but there was no sign of him.
The wind passed by the statue of the saint, but he had no idea that Drippy was trapped inside, trying to climb out.
Finally, the wind gave up.
Poor, poor Drippy.
I'm afraid this time he's really gone.
And the wind sadly blew away.
Inside the statue, meanwhile, Drippy was bravely climbing and slipping, climbing and slipping.
He was getting more and more tired.
And just as he thought he would never make it, he saw a light shining down from above.
It was the tiny crack he had fallen through at the top of the statue.
Filled with hope, Drippy began climbing faster and faster.
He was near the top now, and pretty soon he had reached the crack, and he climbed outside the statue.
He was free.
He could look down and see the people in the park, and the pigeons, and even the park mensch that he should have been sitting on.
Drippy could look down and see the people on the ground, but that also meant that the people could look up and see Drippy.
The crack Drippy was standing on was just below the eye of the saint's statue.
